verdict.rationale: Keycloak documents a client-credentials grant so clients can obtain access 'on behalf of themselves rather than on behalf of a user,' backed by service accounts. Each agent can therefore be its own registered client, created via dynamic client registration or kcadm/Admin REST. Narrow permissions come from role-based and fine-grained resource-level authorization policies, and a token revocation endpoint plus introspection support cutting off access. Missing for 10: agent-specific guidance or examples, evidence that revocation takes effect instantly for self-contained access tokens without introspection, and independent or hands-on corroboration of per-agent least-privilege setups.
